topics.topic: Whether canonical_bytes checks excessive depth before parsing or reports an earlier validation offense in text order
questions: Must an over-depth input always be rejected before parsing, or must parsing determine whether an earlier syntax, duplicate-name, non-finite-number, integer, or lone-surrogate offense occurs first in text order?

Must canonical_bytes always reject excessive depth before parsing, or must it parse far enough to report an earlier malformed value, duplicate member, non-finite number, invalid integer, or lone surrogate as the first offending item?

quotes: MUST raise NonCanonicalValueError, with a reason naming the first offending item in text order
when json_depth of the UTF-8 bytes of json_text exceeds the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant — checked before json_text is parsed, so no parse recurses deeper than that constant —
judgement.why: The first-offense rule requires an earlier textual offense to win, while the mandatory pre-parse depth check requires excessive depth to win before such an offense can be discovered.

topics.topic: Whether counted outputs require json_text to be a string or define a byte-count fallback when it is None
questions: Must json_text be required to be a str for every value output being counted, or must the fallback define what byte count to use when json_text is None?

quotes: The output count is the sum of the canonical bytes (from canonical_bytes) of every value output — for an output whose JSON text canonical_bytes refuses, the UTF-8 bytes of that text as returned — and the bytes of every file output, a many file output counting each element, compared with bounds.output_bytes; it decides whenever the outputs reach the parent, and output over a bound is a failure, never truncated.

contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, an output is not_representable, its JSON text does not give canonical JSON through canonical_bytes, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded.

Returns SandboxResult with the outcome, outputs only for succeeded as PortPayload entries in output port name order (a value as a JsonPayload of its canonical JSON bytes, a file as a FilePayload of its bytes, a many file port as a FileListPayload whose contents are the tuple of its files' bytes in list order), resources_used with elapsed wall_time_ms, peak memory_bytes and the output count as output_bytes, failure_detail, and detail_code None except for cleanup_failed.
ReturnedOutput fields (exact, no others exist): contents: tuple[bytes, ...], form: ReturnedForm, json_text: str | None, port: str
judgement.divergence: One implementer treats a JSON-form output whose json_text is None as a contract violation with a zero-byte contribution; another derives bytes from a representation of None or fails while computing the count. The caller notices a different resources_used.output_bytes or no SandboxResult at all, and a boundary case can also change the outcome between contract_violation and resource_exhausted.
judgement.why: The model permits json_text to be None, but the counting fallback only specifies UTF-8 encoding of the returned text and does not define a count for None.

topics.topic: When and over what body scope json_depth must be measured for an over-ceiling 2xx response
questions: For an over-ceiling 2xx value response, must json_depth be measured on the entire body, requiring reads past the mandated stopping point, or is the depth requirement applied only after the body has been shown not to exceed the response ceiling?

quotes: send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] MUST bound connecting, writing and reading the whole response by one deadline, the monotonic_ns reading taken before connecting plus the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS constant in nanoseconds, held in a local variable only and never stored; each socket wait is given the time left rounded up to whole milliseconds, and the deadline has passed once a later monotonic_ns reading reaches it; the response body is counted after transfer decoding and read at most to one byte past the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant, a body of which that one more byte arrives being over the ceiling and nothing past it being read.

send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is decided in this order, with effect_class read meaning the read column: a failure of name resolution, connection or TLS before the first request byte was written is service_unreachable, attempt not_sent for other classes; a timeout, reset, end of stream before the response is complete (before its headers end, or before the body its Content-Length or chunked framing declares; a body delimited by the connection's close is complete at that close), malformed status line or headers — a status line and header section longer together than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant included —, or only 1xx after the first byte was written is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 3xx is operation_failed with detail redirect_not_followed for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 5xx is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 4xx is operation_refused, attempt not_applied for other classes; 2xx whose body is longer than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant, whatever its output ports, or whose body as read contains the bytes of the credential value sent, searched before parsing, or whose outputs do not fit is contract_violation, attempt applied for other classes; 2xx whose outputs fit is succeeded, attempt applied for other classes.

send_prepared_request: [VALIDATION_ERROR] A 2xx answer with value output ports must be UTF-8 text parsing as one JSON object without duplicate member names, whatever its Content-Type, whose json_depth, measured on the body as a whole before it is parsed, is within the imported RELEASE_CEILING_JSON_DEPTH_MAX constant; each output port takes the member of the same name, which must exist and fit the port by fit_port_value with the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant as size bound, so that a value's own size is judged only by the value_too_large check below, members no port names are ignored, and any failure is contract_violation; after everything else fits, a value whose canonical bytes exceed the imported RELEASE_CEILING_STORED_VALUE_BYTES_MAX constant is contract_violation with detail value_too_large.
judgement.why: The response is first bounded and classified as over-ceiling after reading at most one extra byte; json_depth is measured on the whole body only when the bounded 2xx value response proceeds to output validation.

topics.topic: Whether a refused run may contain waiting points for its waiting elements or must have none
questions: Must a refused run with waiting elements contain one WaitingPoint per waiting element, or must its waiting points be empty?

quotes: A run whose status has ended — refused included — has no waiting point, whatever its elements still wait for (A14 rule 1).
judgement.why: The added passage explicitly requires a refused run to have no waiting points.
